turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How can I help you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi, my son Dave who's 5 years old, who comes to the clinic quite often, has uh, his asthma has been really bad over the past few days. I've tried his puffers, but they're not really helping much, and I'm just worried about him.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So what symptom is he experiencing now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm so, he's just having this wheezing that just doesn't go away, like, I can actually hear it, it's frightening, he's having like he's having difficulties falling asleep, he's just been very irritable, uhm, he didn't go to school yesterday. It's just, yeah, it's just, it seems like, it's just, he's not eating well either.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so yeah, it's been affecting, uh, sleep, appetite, his mood, has he been short of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: If he was like, he said that he was having some difficulty breathing, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, has he, uh, able to talk like in full sentences, like, how is he right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, he's  able to talk in full sentences but he just gets a little bit breathless when he's eating, which I think is probably why he's not eating much. But yeah, he's able to talk, he's not talking much either, just been like, just been in a mood, you know, he gets a little bit breathless when he's crying.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see, and, has he had a cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah he does, he does have a cough, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when did the cough start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I want to say about two days ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and has he been bringing up any sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Or any blood?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No no no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and has the cough been getting any better or any worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's been the same.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uhm, and has he complained of having a sore throat or painful ears?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, he hasn't complained of those.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you noticed any eye redness or or any discharge from his eyes or nose?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and has he been having any chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and you mentioned, uh, a wheeze, have you been able to hear a wheeze like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's usually not this bad.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, has he been having any abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Has he had any urinary problems like, painful when he's going to the bathroom?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, he hasn't complained of anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK, and has he had any diarrhea or Constipation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, has he had any skin changes or rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, I checked for those very carefully. He used to get rashes when he was a child, but no, he doesn't, he doesn't have anything right now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and has he had any muscle aches or joint pains?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, he's just been, he's just been not, he's not been as active as he usually is, so I don't, he hasn't said that any anything in particular about muscle pains, but I don't know if he knows how to, you know? He's just been, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and two days ago, can you think of any triggers like, was there any exposure to dust or smoke or maybe even pets that could have brought this on?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, you know, if I think about it, he did go outside to play with his brother and, I don't know he might have got something out there maybe.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, uh, certainly possible and was it like a particularly cold day?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, it was a very windy, little bit chilly too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And when, like, during the winter time, does cold air trigger attacks for Dave?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about exercise?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think, well, they went outside to play, so I mean he was, uhm, exercise does make it worse sometimes, so it could be that too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and so, has dave been experiencing any other symptoms besides the the wheezing and the irritability and what you've described so far?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so, that's, I think that's it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, you tried some inhalers, how often have you been using them?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, we used his blue inhaler about five times yesterday, and another two or three times earlier today.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you use a spacer?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no we don't. I have to go get that and learn how to use it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, for sure we can go through, Uh, the proper technique, throughout this visit as well, just to review that again.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would love that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: That's great, and has he been using any other medications to help over these last couple of days besides the inhalers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just the inhalers, we've also kept it the usual one, the one that he takes, the other inhaler.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, does he have one that he uses, once, like, he uses daily?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, yeah the one that he uses, I think the orange one.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so he does use a steroid inhaler?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does he have any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no he doesn't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does he have any medical conditions that have diagnosed previously?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just the dermatitis and asthma?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when was his last asthma exacerbation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Last year.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, has he ever needed to be hospitalized for one?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no, no, nothing like that, he's a healthy kid.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that's good, has he had any surgeries before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and in regards to birth history, were there any complications throughout pregnancy or with delivery?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no, everything was normal. He was born via vaginal delivery and no complications. He was a healthy baby.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any concerns with growth or developmental milestones?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, the doc was pretty happy when he did the regular, the checkup and yeah things are good with him, he's a good kid.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Awesome, OK, and could you tell me a little bit about the living situation, like who's the main caregiver and who he's living with?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so he lives with me, his dad and his brother who is 2 years older and he's not going to school right now. We're just keeping him at home due to Covid and trying to do some home schooling. I'm a homemaker, so I do have enough time to spend time with him and his older brother and, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, has anybody in the home been sick, either his brother, yourself, or father?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and anybody, at work or any other places that you maybe traveled to, that, uh, been around anybody who's been sick?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I don't think so. I don't think there was anyone that was sick.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you traveled anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no. We're just staying at home.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are there any pets in the home?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, any carpets or like, uh, curtains or anything like that, covering the windows?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, we got all those removed when he had his big exacerbation last year.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK, and does anybody smoke in the home, either cigarettes or marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, my husband smokes, but he smokes outside, he never smokes in front of the kids.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see, and uh, does anybody in the family, have any heart or lung conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, uhh, I have some, I have high blood pressure but that's it

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any, like, congenital diseases that run in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Or how about any genetic diseases?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Cystic fibrosis or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No no, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uhm, so was there any other, anything else that maybe I forgot to ask about or I'm missing that you'd like to add today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I'm just worried that he's going to have a big asthma attack like last year, I just also want to make sure nothing else is going on and if he can be taken care of and he's just, he's feeling awful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: For sure, yeah, we'll, uh, check his his vital signs and do a physical exam. And it does sound like it could be an asthma exacerbation, and so we can trial some inhaler medications, a little bit different than what you use at home. But also using Ventolin as well and we'll assess the need for potential, uh, antibiotics and also steroid if necessary and if his breathing gets worse or you're starting to hear that the wheezing is getting worse or his work of breathing is becoming more intense then certainly we'll need to add on some oxygen and possibly, some other therapies.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Thank you so much doc.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, thank you.
